items.title: Automated Pallet Racking Inspection: What Changes When Machines Run the Aisles
items.summary: Automated pallet racking inspection is crucial for ensuring the structural soundness and compliance of automated storage systems. Automation makes inspection more important because it removes manual checks that previously caught issues early. Automated systems present unique failure modes, such as rail wear and fatigue, that require specialized inspection. A proper inspection involves a systematic engineering assessment, grading damage based on risk levels, and issuing a detailed report. While monitoring tools can assist, a qualified expert inspection remains necessary to provide the legally required judgment and sign-off.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Automated Pallet Racking Inspection: What Changes When Machines Run the Aisles" reports on the evolving requirements for inspecting automated storage systems due to the introduction of machine-driven operations. Automated systems necessitate specialized inspection methods to identify unique failure modes such as rail wear and fatigue. A proper inspection process involves a systematic engineering assessment where damage is graded according to defined risk levels, culminating in a detailed report. Monitoring tools can provide assistance, but a qualified expert inspection remains necessary to deliver the legally required judgment and official sign-off for automated environments. This development signals an increased demand for specialized, data-driven inspection protocols within the robotics and automation sector.

items.title: NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models
items.summary: NVIDIA expanded the Cosmos platform with new tools, checkpoints, and blueprints to help developers build, evaluate, and deploy world models for physical AI systems. Cosmos Data Factory aids in scaling training data through curated and synthetic data generation for multimodal inputs. The Cosmos Framework provides tools to fine-tune open models and optimize them for deployment using agent skills. New Cosmos 3 Nano models enable testing autonomous policies in simulations, and Cosmos NIM microservices offer faster inference. Ultimately, the platform allows developers to use data factories, frameworks, and microservices to manage the entire world model lifecycle.
items.audio_script: From NVIDIA Blog, "NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models". This report details the expansion of the Cosmos platform with new tools, checkpoints, and blueprints designed to aid developers in building, evaluating, and deploying world models for physical AI systems. The Cosmos Data Factory assists in scaling training data through the generation of curated and synthetic data for multimodal inputs. Furthermore, the Cosmos Framework provides mechanisms to fine-tune open models and optimize them for deployment using agent skills. New Cosmos 3 Nano models facilitate the testing of autonomous policies within simulations, and Cosmos NIM microservices offer increased inference speed. The platform integrates data factories, frameworks, and microservices to manage the complete world model lifecycle. This development signals advancements in the practical deployment capabilities of complex physical AI systems.

items.title: Intramotev to launch autonomous freight rail service in Missouri
items.summary: Intramotev will deploy its TugVolt technology on Missouri’s Columbia Terminal Railroad (COLT) as part of a $16.2 million federal grant. This initiative, selected by the Federal Railroad Administration, aims to advance autonomous freight railcar testing on a working mainline. Two autonomous railcars will be placed on COLT’s 21.4-mile line between Centralia and Columbia, Missouri. Operations will start with remote switching at the Columbia terminal and expand to autonomous freight service. The project will generate a safety record to template autonomous railcar adoption across US short lines.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, Intramotev to launch autonomous freight rail service in Missouri. The initiative, funded by a sixteen point two million dollar federal grant and selected by the Federal Railroad Administration, involves placing two autonomous railcars on the twenty one point four mile line between Centralia and Columbia, Missouri. Operations will commence with remote switching at the Columbia terminal before expanding to autonomous freight service, generating a safety record intended to template autonomous railcar adoption across US short lines. This project establishes a framework for future autonomous rail technology implementation.

items.title: Tesla starts Optimus robot production in California as profit falls 43%
items.summary: Tesla began producing its Optimus humanoid robot in Fremont, California, using a former vehicle manufacturing space. This production marks the first shipment of production-quality Optimus bots, though CEO Elon Musk expects a slow ramp-up due to the product's novelty. Despite this development, the company experienced a 43% drop in profit for the third quarter, driven by heavy investment in Optimus, AI, and autonomous driving. Revenue was largely flat, though the services business showed growth. Net income fell significantly, reflecting the financial strain of pursuing these ambitious projects.
items.audio_script: From TechCrunch - Robotics, "Tesla starts Optimus robot production in California as profit falls 43%". This report details Tesla's commencement of production for its Optimus humanoid robot in Fremont, California, alongside a concurrent decline in profitability. Tesla initiated the manufacturing of the Optimus robot within a former vehicle manufacturing facility. This activity represents the initial shipment of production-quality Optimus units. However, the company anticipates a gradual increase in production volume due to the novelty of the product. Concurrently, Tesla reported a forty-three percent decrease in profit for the third quarter, a result attributed to substantial investment in the Optimus project, artificial intelligence development, and autonomous driving initiatives. Revenue remained relatively stable, while the services segment demonstrated growth. Net income experienced a significant reduction, reflecting the financial demands of these endeavors. This development signals continued heavy investment across the artificial intelligence and robotics sectors.

items.title: Welcome, Voxel!
items.summary: Voxel is a humanoid home robot developed by Tuesday Labs, featuring a boxy yellow head, colorful panels, and Z-shaped legs, standing 150 cm tall and weighing 45 kilograms. It is powered by electric actuators and operates on a proprietary Adaptive Operating System, equipped with stereo RGB cameras for perception. Demonstrated capabilities include obstacle avoidance and sorting goods, which serve as an early foundation for domestic organization and movement. Navigation and manipulation skills are rated low, indicating early development in these areas. Shipping is planned for 2028, and the project emphasizes bringing physical robots into everyday living spaces.

This development signals continued progress in the realization of domestic robotics and embodied AI systems.

items.title: A guide to Day 2 of RoboBusiness 2026
items.summary: Day 2 of RoboBusiness 2026 features a "State of Humanoids" panel discussing humanoid capabilities and challenges. Morning sessions include talks on egocentric robot learning, China's AI ecosystem, and the challenges of physical AI in real-world applications. Afternoon sessions cover topics like scaling physical AI, policy discussions on robotics, and real-time robot troubleshooting. Attendees can also visit the Exhibitor Hall for demos and startup showcases.

items.title: AGCO Digit pilot targets parts handling at Kansas factory
items.summary: AGCO will pilot Agility Robotics’ Digit humanoid at its Hesston, Kansas factory starting in 2027 to handle parts sorting and tote placement. The pilot will occur in an existing agricultural equipment factory with over 1,100 employees. The goal is to automate repetitive, physically demanding tasks to improve operational efficiency and reduce employee strain without major infrastructure changes. The deployment tests the robot's ability to perform useful work in human-centric workflows. Digit is engineered to work safely alongside people, and the Arc cloud platform allows for fleet management without extensive infrastructure overhauls.
items.audio_script: From Humanoid.guide, "AGCO Digit pilot targets parts handling at Kansas factory". This report details an upcoming pilot program for the Digit humanoid robot to automate parts handling in an existing agricultural equipment factory. The pilot aims to test the robot's capability in sorting and tote placement tasks within a human-centric workflow to enhance operational efficiency. The trial is scheduled to commence in 2027 at the Hesston, Kansas facility, which employs over one thousand one hundred individuals. The deployment involves utilizing the Digit to handle repetitive and physically demanding tasks without requiring major infrastructure modifications. The system is designed to operate safely alongside personnel, and the associated Arc cloud platform facilitates fleet management without significant infrastructural overhauls. The results will provide data on practical application of humanoid robotics in manufacturing environments. Future developments in collaborative robotics will depend on the successful outcomes of this type of integration.

items.title: Real-Time Ground Normal Vector Estimation for Spherical Mobile 3D Mapping using LiDAR-Inertial Odometry
items.summary: Accurate ground plane normal estimation is crucial for odometry in spherical mobile mapping systems due to rapid rotations and limited coverage. Two RANSAC methods are proposed: single-scan estimation and multi-step validation. LiDAR-Inertial Odometry (LIO) estimation, utilizing a global 3D map, was found to significantly outperform single-scan methods in accuracy and robustness. Integrating these ground normal estimates into the motion model enhances pose estimation for autonomous navigation. This work demonstrates a method for real-time estimation using LIO for spherical mapping.

items.title: Warping the Workspace: Expanding Visual Access with Adjustable Reach Mapping for Humanoid Teleoperation
items.summary: First-person humanoid teleoperation is improved by tying access to side and rear targets to operator rotation. The research presents coupled visual-motor remapping, specifically pairing a panoramic azimuth warp with an inverse upper-limb yaw transform. A working prototype incorporates Global Zoom (GZ) and Focus+Context (F+C) mechanisms for visual access. In a study, Global Zoom yielded the highest completion count, while Focus+Context was preferred by a majority of participants. This suggests that the optimal mapping strategy depends on the specific task requirements.

items.title: Human-Robot Interaction via Meta-Learning Based Mode Recognition and Adaptive Control
items.summary: A novel framework using meta-learning is proposed to improve human-robot interaction (HRI) by recognizing interaction modes without predefined thresholds. A neural network, trained via meta-learning incorporating force-dependent parameters, recognizes human intention with high accuracy for both active and passive modes. An adaptive meta-learning controller is introduced to compensate for human disturbances and adapt to varying interaction forces online. A multiple-trajectory meta-learning algorithm jointly learns environment representation and force parameters for handling unmodeled dynamics. This approach results in robust control performance and reliable mode recognition for safe physical HRI.

items.title: Learning-Enhanced Observer for Sensorless Task-Null-Space Compliant Control
items.summary: A novel framework is presented integrating a wrench observer and a hybrid pose and force controller for physical Human-Robot Interaction (pHRI). A neural network is used to enhance the observer by compensating for friction and unmodeled dynamics. Task-null-space decomposition is applied to separate joint velocities and reduce human disturbance effects on the observer. This method achieves robust wrench estimation and accurate pose/force tracking without relying on force/torque sensors. The approach provides an effective solution for pHRI on platforms lacking such sensors.

items.title: VeriCalib: Verifiable Target-Based LiDAR-Camera Calibration
items.summary: VeriCalib addresses the limitations of traditional target-based LiDAR-camera calibration by formulating it as a verifiable estimation problem. It introduces a two-level extrinsic compensation mechanism to separately correct residual errors and parameter level errors. The method assesses calibration quality using a structured covariance that propagates uncertainty from sensor features with a known-geometry prior. This approach decouples rotation and translation uncertainty to guide data collection towards the weakest direction. Finally, it establishes a calibration state based on internal and cross-view checks to indicate whether the calibration result should be accepted.

items.title: T-WLA: Bridging Slow Vision and Fast Touch
items.summary: T-WLA is a world-language-action architecture designed to bridge slow vision processing with fast tactile feedback in contact-rich manipulation. It utilizes shared visual memory to guide both action generation and tactile correction simultaneously. The visual branch integrates visual input with task instructions and history to form a memory for action generation. This memory is cached for a lightweight tactile editor that predicts residual corrections based on active actions and incoming touch. Evaluation on real-world tasks shows T-WLA reduces finger-joint MPJPE by 30% and achieves a 50.0% success rate in manipulation.

items.title: Real2Sem2Real: 3D Semantic Augmentations for Robot Learning from a Single Human RGB Demonstration
items.summary: The Real2Sem2Real pipeline transforms a single human RGB demonstration into thousands of robot demonstrations through 3D semantic augmentations. It utilizes DINOv3-distilled Gaussian splats to track object poses and aligns digital cousins based on semantic information. This process maps the human hand to feasible robot grasps, generating over 2,000 episodes in a short time. Policies trained on this data achieve performance comparable to teleoperation across diverse object instances. The method effectively enables robot learning from minimal human input without requiring depth sensing or complex setups.

items.title: inr2action: Encoding Robot Episodes as Neural Implicit Representations for Recall and Action
items.summary: Long-horizon robotic operation requires a memory framework that stores episodes as separable objects using neural implicit representations. A neural implicit representation is fitted to episode video from a shared initialization, where the resulting weight delta constitutes the memory, independent of episode length. A learned projector maps this weight delta into token embeddings, which condition a language model for question answering and a decoder for joint command regression. This method decouples memory cost from time horizon, enabling scalable streaming memory. Empirical results show that this approach significantly outperforms methods without the meta-learned initialization.

items.title: Learning Dynamic Games for Cooperative Iterative Tasks
items.summary: The framework learns dynamic games for cooperative, iterative tasks involving multiple agents with shared constraints. It utilizes previously executed feasible trajectories to construct a sampled joint safe set and player-specific cost-to-go functions for nonlinear games. Agents jointly select a terminal state and Generalized Nash equilibrium at each step, adopting a new solution only if a cooperative acceptance rule is met. This method guarantees recursive feasibility and can ensure that each player's cost is non-increasing across iterations. The framework accommodates individual requirements like weighted costs and Nash bargaining criteria.
